description: Model 2 visual label (not a confirmed cause): A generic fungal-disease class for curry leaf (Murraya koenigii). The label should not be interpreted as one specific fungus unless the source dataset confirms it. A well-documented fungal leaf disease of curry leaf is anthracnose/leaf spot caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides; powdery mildew has also been reported on curry leaf. For a generic visual class, the safest wording is therefore 'fungal infection' rather than assigning a pathogen from the image alone. A similar appearance may also arise from: Possible fungal leaf spots/anthracnose/mildew; sooty deposits on honeydew; dust; abiotic discoloration. Colletotrichum leaf spot on curry leaf is specifically reported to begin as small circular dark spots that enlarge and may develop visible black fungal fruiting bodies.
healthy_difference: Healthy curry leaf leaflets are intact, evenly green and free from necrotic spots, expanding brown/black lesions, yellow lesion halos, fungal fruiting bodies, powdery surface growth, tip blight and premature drying.
medicinal_use_instruction: Do not use curry leaves with visible active fungal infection, mould-like growth, substantial necrotic spotting or blight for medicinal preparation.
